sentences.text: Corynebacterium accolens is a lipid-requiring species described as benign and as a common colonizer of the human nose.
It is listed among the most common human nasal Corynebacterium species, a genus reported to be globally ubiquitous in human nasal microbiota across the lifespan.
A study reported that it hydrolyses human skin surface triacylglycerols using the lipase LipS1 and releases oleic acid, which inhibits pneumococcus.
The same study observed that Corynebacterium species were overrepresented in children free of Streptococcus pneumoniae, a common pediatric nasal colonizer.
Another study described it as the predominant species of the healthy human nasal microbiota, with its relative abundance decreased in the context of chronic rhinosinusitis.
